memory_update.text: HD should remain a reference anchor only: it is the dominant public pro/DIY context name and now owns SRS and GMS, but its mega-cap retail exposure makes it less useful for underfollowed discovery.

QXO is a high-priority direct distributor candidate for the housing repair/remodel inputs node because Beacon and Kodiak give it roofing, waterproofing, lumber, and building-products distribution exposure; later layers must stress-test leverage, integration risk, and organic growth.
WSO is a direct HVAC replacement distribution candidate; the key bottleneck lens is contractor access, local inventory, A2L refrigerant transition, and replacement demand versus new housing weakness.

SITE is a mid-cap underfollowed candidate tied to landscape and irrigation maintenance/repair distribution; later layers should separate resilient maintenance demand from discretionary outdoor upgrade exposure.

Several formerly clean public specialty distributors are no longer standalone: Beacon is now inside QXO, and GMS is now inside Home Depot/SRS. This reduces the number of pure small/mid-cap public distributor targets and makes second-order suppliers/components more important in later passes.

WSO should be retained as the HVAC/R distribution reference anchor for repair/replacement economics, but not treated as the main underfollowed alpha target due to large-cap status and higher visibility.

NX is a high-priority underfollowed Layer 1B candidate because it sits below visible window/door OEMs as a component supplier; later layers must verify repair-and-replacement exposure and post-Tyman integration quality.

ROCK is a plausible underfollowed residential-components candidate tied to roofing, ventilation, flashing, gutters and exterior repair SKUs; evidence gap is the exact split between repair/remodel and new construction.
SITE broadens the node into outdoor repair, irrigation, hardscape and property-maintenance inputs; it should be tested for maintenance resilience versus discretionary repair/upgrade weakness.
For housing repair/remodel chokepoints, the most promising underfollowed mappings appear to be component suppliers and pro-channel distributors rather than consumer-facing retailers or homebuilders.

Need a later pass on plumbing/electrical/HVAC component manufacturers and specialty distributors below $10B market cap, including refrigerant, code-compliant electrical, pumps, valves, water heaters and restoration inputs.

CSW should be tracked as a mid-cap underfollowed contractor-SKU supplier for HVAC/R, plumbing, electrical, sealants and building safety products; verify organic Contractor Solutions growth and replacement/MRO mix.

SITE should be tracked as an exterior-property repair/maintenance distributor with strong branch density and recurring contractor interactions; verify maintenance plus repair/upgrade resilience versus new-construction and existing-home-sales sensitivity.
Installer capacity is investable through public installation platforms such as IBP, but R&R purity may be limited because new construction remains a major revenue driver.
Need a follow-up search for pure-play HVAC, plumbing, roofing and restoration distributors that remain public after recent consolidation involving Beacon, GMS, SRS/Home Depot and FBM/Lowe's.

BXC should remain on the Layer 1 watchlist as a small-cap underfollowed specialty building-products distributor, but later layers must separate repair/remodel specialty exposure from commodity structural-product cyclicality.
CSW is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate because HVAC/R and plumbing repair/replacement exposure is embedded inside niche contractor products rather than obvious housing-retail categories.

HAYW is a second-order housing R&R adjacency through installed pool equipment aftermarket demand; the key falsification test is whether aftermarket share and dealer sell-through remain resilient during weak outdoor discretionary spending.

Pro-facing distribution density and jobsite fulfillment appear to be validated chokepoints, supported by large strategic acquisitions of SRS, GMS, and Foundation Building Materials by home-improvement leaders.

Next pass should search for public micro/small-cap suppliers of code-compliant plumbing/HVAC consumables, restoration materials, roofing accessories, water heaters, door/window components, and contractor software because these may be more obscure than distributors.

node: Housing repair-and-remodel inputs, specialty building products, replacement components, and installer-facing distribution
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for repair-and-remodel inputs and installer-facing distribution. The cleanest public exposures are specialty trade distributors that sit behind contractors rather than consumer-facing retailers. Home Depot is included only as a reference anchor because it now owns SRS and GMS; the discovery lane emphasizes QXO, Watsco, and SiteOne as more direct distribution-network plays tied to roofing, HVAC/R replacement, and landscape/irrigation maintenance or repair demand. Expanded the housing repair-and-remodel input node into a compact two-lane universe. The reference anchor is Watsco for HVAC/R replacement-parts distribution. The underfollowed lane emphasizes one- or two-step-away suppliers and distributors: Quanex for window/door components, Gibraltar for residential roofing/ventilation/drainage-adjacent building products, and SiteOne for professional landscape, irrigation, hardscape, and maintenance inputs. These are not recommendations; they are Layer 1B research candidates whose survival depends on later verification of replacement-driven demand, margin resilience, channel density, and exposure to discretionary remodel cycles. Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around repair-and-remodel inputs and contractor-facing fulfillment rather than consumer-facing retailers. The strongest underfollowed angle is not Home Depot/Lowe's traffic itself, but branch density, pro-contractor relationships, replacement SKUs, HVAC/plumbing/electrical consumables, exterior-property maintenance, and installer labor availability.
